tagline: One road reaches Edisto Beach, where access once followed the tide.
intro: South Carolina Highway 174 provides the only road access to Edisto Beach, crossing Edisto Island through Charleston County. The beach town occupies the developed coastal part of the island in Colleton County, with Edisto Beach State Park along its north and east sides.

In the 1920s, South Carolina residents came to build rough retreats on Edisto Island and Edisto Beach. Access then depended on low tide: travelers drove or rode across the marsh on beds of oyster shells. In 1935, the Edisto Company donated land for a state park, which the Civilian Conservation Corps developed.

From US 17 at Osborn, Highway 174 runs across the island to Edisto Beach, a distance of 24 miles. At the park, trails lead through maritime forest to a shell midden and an 1850 survey monument. The town beyond is separated from the rest of Colleton County by the tidal South Edisto River.

moments.title: Edisto Beach State Park
moments.text: Edisto Beach State Park’s trails pass through maritime forest to traces of two very different kinds of work. One destination is a Native American shell midden; another is a monument placed by surveyor Alexander Bache in 1850. Bache’s team marked each end of its Coast Survey baseline with a buried granite block and a granite monument above it. The park itself was developed by the Civilian Conservation Corps on land donated by the Edisto Company in 1935. Many original CCC buildings remain standing and in use. The Edisto Interpretive Center includes interactive exhibits explaining the ACE Basin estuarine reserve.

moments.title: Spanish Mount Point
moments.text: Spanish Mount is an oyster-and-clam shell midden in Edisto Beach State Park. Water and marsh border it on three sides. The deposit accumulated during a short occupation between 2200 and 1800 BC. It measures about 27 meters long and 3 meters high. The site entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1974.

moments.title: Edisto Beach
moments.text: Edisto Beach belongs to Colleton County, but its only road connection runs through Charleston County. Town limits cover the developed coastal area within Colleton County; most of Edisto Island lies outside the town in Charleston County. The distinction matters on the approach: Highway 174 crosses the island, while the state park borders the beach town on the north and east.
